# jev-watch

> A watchdog for AI coding agents. jev-watch runs Codex, OpenCode or any coding CLI in the background, detects when the agent loops on the same error, stalls, or drifts off task, stops it, and prints a short report so a lead agent (such as Claude Code) can send a correction that resumes the same Codex/OpenCode session. It uses free local rules plus TypeSafe's Jev decision model (sub-second, available on OpenRouter). Node 20+, zero runtime dependencies, MIT.

Use it when one orchestrator agent delegates coding work to cheaper worker agents and you want to stop paying the orchestrator to poll worker logs.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/polaminggkub-debug/jev-watch/blob/main/README.md): install, usage, report format, FAQ
- [Architecture](https://github.com/polaminggkub-debug/jev-watch/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md): layers and enforced guard rules

## Quick reference

- Install as a Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add polaminggkub-debug/jev-watch` then `claude plugin install jev-watch@jev-watch`. Its hook wraps every `codex exec` / `opencode run` automatically.

- Run and watch: `jev-watch -- codex exec "<task>"` or `jev-watch -- opencode run "<task>"`
- Resume after a stop: `jev-watch --resume <runId> "<correction>"`
- Watch an existing log: `jev-watch --log <file> --pid <pid> --task "<task>"`
- Exit codes: 0 done, 1 worker failed, 2 stopped by watcher, 3 out of corrections, 64 usage
- API key: JEV_WATCH_API_KEY, else OPENROUTER_API_KEY, else TYPESAFE_API_KEY; `--no-jev` for local rules only
